analysis.title: Memory Market Update: 3Q26 results wrap and 4Q26/2027 outlook, our thoughts on memory share prices
key_insights: JPM reads the memory makers' 3Q26 results as positively biased: EPS and margin beats despite F/X headwinds, pricing upside, a successful HBM price negotiation and volume delivery. Company-specific misses were Samsung Electronics' lack of an imminent shareholder return and Kioxia's weak CY4Q26 guidance, which JPM calls temporary.
JPM expects bottom-up memory supply/demand to stay very solid through 2028E. End demand is mixed: steady hyperscaler AI capex growth (B2B) versus a harder PC/mobile market (B2C).
DRAM ASP rose 23% Q/Q in 3Q26 against JPM's high-teens to 20% expectation. Makers guided 4Q bit growth up by double digits Q/Q. JPM estimates the industry exits 2026 with high-20% y/y bit growth.

Memory makers began shipping HBM4 and guided to an HBM4 bit/revenue crossover in 3Q26/4Q26E. They also guided to a narrowing profitability gap versus conventional DRAM into 2027E after the price negotiation.

JPM had warned that an aggressive HBM ASP increase could be double-edged (stronger memory earnings versus demand destruction). It sees smooth negotiation as implying manageable customer risk and models a +96% HBM ASP increase in 2027E.

Memory makers unanimously said demand outstrips supply beyond 2027, and some guided 2027 memory as effectively sold out. JPM expects this to give relief once earnings prove resilient amid AI funding and sustainability worries.

NAND: JPM sees no near-term downcycle, contrary to market belief in a price downcycle from 4Q26E driven by inventory buildup and China capacity additions. It attributes Kioxia's December-quarter guidance miss to company-specific pull-ins into the September quarter and push-outs into the March quarter.

The NAND bit growth outlook for 2027E diverges: Micron guides as high as mid-20% and SK hynix high-teens. JPM puts this down to differences in capacity ramp timing. KV-cache offload eSSD demand is ongoing, and China NAND makers focus on consumer applications, a limited threat to international eSSD demand.

Long-term agreement (LTA) coverage is expanding. Every memory maker guided 2027 as part of LTA contracts with more customers, and some contracts run beyond 2030. Makers guide at least 50% coverage in 2027/28, and Samsung targets 60-70% of capacity by 2030.

JPM ranks 2026E shareholder return execution SK hynix first, Samsung Electronics second and Kioxia third. SK hynix lifted its return pool from under 50% to over 50% of FCF and plans W100T in 2026. Samsung stuck to about 50% of FCF. Kioxia lacks an imminent buyback.

Among US names, Sandisk announced a TSR near 88% of FCF in CY3Q, though small in absolute size. Micron shared little on buybacks or dividends because of the CHIPS Act. Its buyback authorization unlocks on Dec 9.

Server mix is rising: JPM estimates server share of DRAM sales (server DRAM plus HBM) at 60%+ in 2026 versus 50%+ in 2025, and 70%+ in 2027E. Server demand is crowding out smartphone and PC supply, which JPM expects to show up as price hikes and unit declines in B2C, with concentration risk worth monitoring.

Hyperscaler capex rose +87% y/y in 3Q (~US$217bn) and JPM's US hardware team expects tier-1/tier-2 AI capex of $1.5trn in 2027E versus ~$800bn in 2026E. Cloud AI revenue accelerated (Azure +48%, GCP +103%, AWS +39%).

Consumer devices are under pressure from memory costs: Intel guided PC unit TAM down double digits y/y in 2026/27E, Apple guided its Dec-quarter gross margin to 45-46% on memory pricing, and Intel expects a PC correction into 1Q27, maybe 2Q.

Memory trades below 3.5x 2027E P/E against a 98% 2026-28E EPS CAGR, versus 6-7x previously. JPM says the market is pricing an AI-funding and power-bottleneck driven downcycle as early as 1H27E, and EPS cuts are unlikely in the next 6 months because LTAs and prepayments buffer earnings.

Memory stocks are down 45% from their 2026 peak versus SOX at -29%. JPM stays Overweight on SK hynix, Samsung Electronics and Kioxia and expects range-bound trading near term for lack of catalysts. Its three-month preference by shareholder return upside is SK hynix, then Samsung, then Kioxia.

market_movers.rationale: Top pick on three-month shareholder return upside. JPM says SK hynix is executing most smoothly on TSR and cites successful HBM price negotiation. The $260 target is from the rating history table (28-Oct-26).

Samsung Electronics (005930.KS, no US listing) ranks second on shareholder return. It kept its roughly 50% FCF payout with no pool increase at 3Q26 earnings, and JPM expects the return catalyst back in January 2027. The target is from the rating history table (30-Jul-26).

Kioxia (285A.T, no US listing) ranks third on shareholder return, with no imminent buyback and an unclear definition of excess cash. JPM views the weak December-quarter guidance as temporary and expects CY1Q27 growth above seasonal.

sector_views.rationale: JPM sees solid supply/demand through 2028E, LTA coverage expanding and a valuation below 3.5x 2027E P/E. It expects range-bound shares near term and an attractive medium-term risk-reward.
Memory shortages and price hikes are weighing on PC and smartphone units, with server demand crowding out consumer supply.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 DRAM ASP rose 23% Q/Q (reported, industry) versus JPM's estimate of high-teens to 20% Q/Q. Industry DRAM bit growth was +6% Q/Q and 4Q26E bit guidance is +mid-teens% (JPM estimate after penciling in company guidance).

Samsung Electronics 3Q26 DRAM: bit growth low-to-mid % Q/Q, ASP about +20% Q/Q, 4Q26E bit guidance mid-to-high-10%. SK hynix DRAM: bits about +10% Q/Q, ASP high-20% Q/Q, 4Q26E bits mid-20% Q/Q. Micron (August quarter) DRAM: bits +MSD%, ASP high-10%.
NAND 3Q26 (reported): industry bits +7% Q/Q and ASP +7% Q/Q. Samsung ASP +high-10%, SK hynix ASP +mid-20%, Micron ASP about +30%, Kioxia ASP about +mid-20% with 4Q bits flat Q/Q, Sandisk ASP +HSD%.

Kioxia's CY4Q26 guidance was weak (guidance miss versus expectations). JPM attributes it to pull-ins into the September quarter and push-outs into the March quarter and expects CY1Q27 growth above seasonal and ahead of peers.

Samsung Electronics 3Q26A: no lift to the shareholder return pool, with the ~50% FCF payout and W90-110T FY26E return unchanged. SK hynix guided HBM4 volume shipments began with yields above plan. Micron guided that the majority of 2027 HBM bits are contracted at significantly higher prices.

TSMC 3Q26A (reported): revenue +16% Q/Q and +41% Y/Y, gross margin 66.4%, operating margin 58.7%, HPC 68% of sales. 4Q26 guidance (company guidance, not yet reported): revenue $52.3-$54.3bn and gross margin 65-67%. 2026 USD revenue growth raised to ~44%.

Intel 3Q26A (reported): revenue $16.5bn (+21%), non-GAAP EPS $0.52 versus its $0.38 guide, DCAI $7.3bn (+78%), CCPG $8.1bn (-5% y/y). 4Q guidance (company guidance) is revenue $15-16bn and CCPG down more than 20% Q/Q.

Apple 3Q26A (reported): revenue $114.5bn (+12%), iPhone $57.6bn (+17%), gross margin 47.9% including about 1pt tariff refund. Dec-quarter gross margin guided 45-46% versus 46.3% consensus, with Mac and iPad supply constrained on memory.

Hyperscaler CY3Q26A (reported): Microsoft capex $45.2bn, Azure $33.2bn (+48%). Alphabet capex $51.4bn, Google Cloud $30.7bn (+103%). Amazon cash capex $75.9bn, AWS $46.0bn (+39.3%). Meta capex $34.9bn, revenue $64.6bn (+26%).

Hyperscaler 2026 capex guidance (company guidance): Microsoft cut to about $170bn CY from $175bn, Alphabet held $195-205bn, Amazon held about $220bn, Meta narrowed to $135-145bn with the low end raised.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Firm server demand and rising 2027E spend support memory demand.

macro_indicators.interpretation: JPM expects AI capex growth to offset B2C earnings weakness at memory makers.
Pricing beat JPM's high-teens to 20% estimate, driving mild earnings beats.
Implied by 4Q guidance of mid-teens% Q/Q bit growth.
Valuation implies the market is pricing a downcycle by 1H27E despite no EPS cuts.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight SK hynix (SKHY), first in JPM's three-month order of preference by shareholder return upside, ahead of Samsung Electronics and Kioxia
trade_ideas.rationale: SK hynix is executing most smoothly on shareholder return, which JPM calls an important barometer for valuation multiples.
trade_ideas.risk: Range-bound trading near term because of no imminent catalysts, and AI funding or monetization concerns.

risk_factors: AI funding and sustainability concerns, and AI monetization doubts, could drive a memory downcycle as early as 1H27E.
Power bottlenecks for AI data centers could slow capex and memory demand.
An aggressive HBM ASP increase could cause demand destruction at end customers.
B2C weakness (PC and mobile) from memory price hikes and unit corrections, and server concentration risk.
NAND price growth deceleration, inventory buildup and China capacity additions.
HBM de-spec risk, cited as one reason memory shares de-rated.
Company-specific: Samsung's limited near-term shareholder return upside and Kioxia's lack of an imminent buyback.
charts_described: Figure 9 and Table 6 as annotated in the text: memory stocks have corrected 45% from the 2026 peak versus SOX at -29%.
Table 6 memory valuation: average 2026E P/E 12.9x and 2027E 3.6x, average 2026-28E EPS CAGR 98%. Kioxia shows the highest 2026E P/E at 35.9x and SK hynix the lowest at 3.9x.
vol_and_positioning: Memory stocks are down 45% from the 2026 peak versus SOX at -29%, and JPM says the bearish sentiment will likely continue until AI funding and AI monetization concerns are resolved. SK hynix fell further after its 3Q26 results despite the return announcement.
Memory shares traded at 6-7x P/E before de-rating to below 3.5x 2027E P/E, while EPS estimates have not been cut. JPM frames the debate as 'too-cheap to ignore' versus 'it is cheap for a reason.'
geopolitical: China NAND makers are described as focused on consumer-related applications, posing limited threat to international eSSD demand, per JPM's checks.
Micron's shareholder return disclosure is limited by CHIPS Act conditions.

tension_points.bull_case: Memory trades below 3.5x 2027E P/E against a 98% 2026-28E EPS CAGR, with demand outstripping supply beyond 2027 and LTAs and prepayments protecting earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: The market anticipates an AI funding and power-bottleneck driven memory downcycle as early as 1H27E, so the stocks are cheap for a reason.
tension_points.what_invalidates: EPS cuts within the next 6 months, which JPM considers unlikely because the supply-demand gap is too wide to narrow quickly.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM sees resilient NAND fundamentals with no price cuts near term, ongoing KV-cache offload eSSD demand and limited threat from China NAND makers.
tension_points.bear_case: Market belief in a NAND price downcycle from 4Q26E driven by inventory buildup and China capacity additions, with Kioxia's weak December-quarter guidance and genuine price growth deceleration.

tension_points.bull_case: Smooth HBM price negotiation implies largely manageable risk at end customers and stronger memory earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: An aggressive HBM ASP increase could cause demand destruction at end customers.
